sheet_prompts.a:
STYLE REFERENCE (attached image): The attached image is an already-approved unit from the SAME game (warrior). Match ONLY its hand-painted 2D art style, bold dark ink outline weight, flat cel shading with soft highlights, earthy colour richness, silhouette readability at 48 pixels, flat #FF00FF magenta background, and saturated pure-red (#E01010) team-colour convention. DO NOT copy that character, silhouette, outfit, weapon, mount, or vehicle — draw a completely different unit matching the specification below.

ERA / VISUAL THEME: Early gunpowder-era musket infantry (Era 5): clean hand-painted historical 2D strategy art matching the Pikeman, Swordsman and Axeman sprites.

I am making art for ONE unit in a family-friendly historical strategy game. Draw ONE image: the master design of this unit.
Every later image of this unit will be drawn from it, and the game will animate this drawing by cutting it into parts, so it
must follow the pose rules exactly.

THE UNIT: Musketeer. A 17th-century musketeer: a friendly adult man with a long face, neat dark-brown moustache and short beard, brown eyes and strong eyebrows, wearing a wide-brimmed brown felt hat with a small feather, a bold red wool coat to mid-thigh with plain brass buttons over a tan linen shirt with a white collar, a brown leather bandolier across his chest hung with small wooden powder charges, a wide brown leather belt, dark wool breeches, light stockings and brown leather shoes with simple buckles. He holds a long wooden-stocked matchlock musket with a dark iron barrel in both hands.

STYLE: clean hand-painted 2D game art, bold dark outline, flat cel shading with soft highlights, earthy saturated palette,
friendly readable proportions that still read when the unit is 48 pixels tall. No photorealism, no 3D-render look, no pixel art.

VIEW: strict side view, facing RIGHT. The whole unit is inside the image with empty space of about a tenth of the image on
every side. No ground, floor, shadow, scenery, text, labels, border or effects.

BACKGROUND: one completely flat, uniform solid pure magenta (#FF00FF) background filling the entire image behind the unit. NO transparency checkerboard, NO grey-and-white grid, NO gradient, NO drop shadow, NO ambient glow, NO vignette, NO soft semi-transparent edges. Every outline, smoke puff, flame, dust cloud, or effect must be 100% solid, opaque, and hard-edged with a clean dark ink outline against the #FF00FF magenta so nothing blends into purple. Put nothing magenta, pink, or purple anywhere on the unit.

TEAM COLOUR: paint his coat saturated pure red (#E01010). That is the ONLY red or red-orange anywhere in the image.
Everything else (skin, hair, leather, wood, metal, stains) is brown, tan, grey, black, white, bronze or dull dark maroon. The game recolours that red to
each player's colour, so any other red would change colour too.

POSE FOR ANIMATION (the most important part):
- Standing at rest, weight on both feet, both feet flat on the ground with a gap of about one boot length between them,
  knees straight, body upright.
- The garment ends above the knee, so both legs show below the hem as two separate shapes that do not touch.
- Nothing hangs in front of or behind the legs below the hem: shield, cloak, quiver, scabbard, pouches and sash all stay above
  the hem.
- He holds the musket across his body at the ready: near hand gripping the stock just behind the lock at chest height, far hand supporting the barrel ahead of it, the barrel angled up to the right and the butt held at his hip, so the whole musket stays at or above his belt, completely clear of his legs and shoes, with background visible between the musket and his legs.

Generate the image now with crisp opaque edges on flat solid #FF00FF magenta.

DAMAGE (4 frames, a grid of 2 by 2): the master's standing pose four times, the unit progressively hurt. Keep the legs and
   feet EXACTLY where they are in the master in all four frames (the game builds the walk from each of these drawings); any
   slump shows only in the head, shoulders and arms. In every frame the two legs are separate posts with a visible gap of
   empty background between them from the boots up, both feet flat on one ground line; mud, bandages and torn cloth never
   join the legs. Keep any prop the unit holds a hand's width clear of the
   boots. Keep the same headgear in all four frames (frame 3 may dent it) and every prop whole in frames 1 to 3 (frame 4 may
   break it, still held). (1) healthy, identical to the master; (2) light: dirt on clothes and legs,
   one clear slash across the garment, a scuffed hem; (3) serious: torn garment and sleeve, a dented hat brim, a scuffed coat and a scratched musket stock, a few dark-maroon
   stains, messy hair; (4) critical: bandages on chest and forearm, a bruised face, a torn hat brim, a ripped coat sleeve, a cracked musket stock, still held in his hands, a tired slumped
   head and shoulders. Each frame must look clearly worse than the one before at a glance.

NO transparency checkerboard, NO grey-and-white grid, NO gradient, NO drop shadow, NO ambient glow, NO vignette, NO soft semi-transparent edges. Every outline, smoke puff, flame, dust cloud, or effect must be 100% solid, opaque, and hard-edged with a clean dark ink outline against the #FF00FF magenta so nothing blends into purple. Put nothing magenta, pink, or purple anywhere on the unit.
- Paint his coat saturated pure red (#E01010), exactly as in the master; it is the ONLY bright red anywhere in the image. Wounds, stains, rust, and fire are dark maroon, brown, grey, yellow-orange, or black — never bright red. Family-friendly, no blood and no gore.
- No text, labels, numbers, boxes, borders, grid lines, ground planes, or shadows.

Keep the exact same face as the master and frames 1-3: same long face, same neat dark-brown moustache and short beard, same brown eyes and eyebrows, same nose. Show critical damage only through a small bruise on the cheek, a bandage on the forearm and torn coat, never by changing the facial features, hair, or the hat shape.
